note_on_method: Each venue page rests on two City of Rockville pages - the Pickleball Courts and Programs page, whose table under "Outdoor Pickleball Courts" counts the courts and answers the lighting question row by row, and the park's own place page, which gives the address under an "Address" heading and describes the park - plus the US Census address geocoder for the county and the postcode. Where the City is silent, on price, on surface, on nets at three venues, these pages record the silence.

slots.description:
Four dedicated pickleball courts, lit, in a 7.5-acre sports park on Twinbrook Parkway, open dawn to dusk and until 10 p.m. under the lights.

The count is the City's own cell in its outdoor-courts table: "4 Dedicated Pickleball Courts", Lighted "Yes". Dedicated is the word that matters. Most of Rockville's pickleball is lines painted on tennis courts, and Broome is one of two venues in the city where every court was built for the game, with no tennis lines to read past and no tennis net at the wrong height. The park's own page says the same thing from the other side - "four pickleball courts" beside "two tennis courts" - and its accessible-features table repeats it: "Four accessible pickleball courts."

The City describes the park as "a 7.5-acre sports paradise next to the site of the former Edwin W. Broome Junior High School", with two lighted premier baseball fields, a futsal court and a playground. The premier fields are fenced, locked and "primarily used for league play", so on a league night the park will be busy whether or not the courts are.
slots.getting_there:
751 Twinbrook Parkway, Rockville, MD 20851, under the "Address" heading on the park's page. The US Census address geocoder matched that address at house-number level, as the City writes it, and placed it in Montgomery County inside the incorporated place Rockville city, in the same postcode the City prints.

Parking is stated: the City says there is "plenty of parking" and counts "Six accessible parking spaces." in its accessible-features table, with an accessible path from the parking to the playground. There are drinking fountains and park benches. Restrooms are not listed among the park's features, and this page does not add them.
slots.what_to_expect:
Four real pickleball courts and a stated lighting answer, which in Rockville means a court you can use after work. The City's rule for every court in its table is "Courts are open from dawn to dusk and are available on a first-come, first-served basis", and for this row it adds "Lighted courts close at 10 p.m." Four courts is enough for a rotation rather than a single game.

Two things the City states cut the other way. "City recreation programs have priority over the use of the courts, so some may be reserved for class use and closed to the public" - the City runs adult, youth, family and private lessons and a league, and the row carries a "View Schedule" link that this page has not read, so when a court is closed for class is not published here. And the row says nothing about nets: the bring-your-own-net note that sits on Rockville's striped courts is absent from the dedicated ones, so whether a net is on the court is not stated either way.

No price is stated anywhere, and no surface. Every court in the table is outdoor by the City's heading.

faqs.a: Four, all dedicated pickleball courts in the City's words: "4 Dedicated Pickleball Courts". The park's own page counts them the same way, as "four pickleball courts" and "Four accessible pickleball courts."
Yes. The Lighted column of the City's table reads Yes for this row, and the City adds that "Lighted courts close at 10 p.m."

faqs.a: Not stated. The City's row says only "4 Dedicated Pickleball Courts", without the bring-your-own-net note it attaches to its striped courts, so no net answer is published here.
Not stated. No price and no word free appear on the City's pickleball page or the park's page. Courts are first-come, first-served, with City programmes taking priority.
Yes, stated by the City: "plenty of parking", with six accessible parking spaces counted in the park's accessible-features table.

slots.description:
Two pickleball courts painted on one tennis court in a 5.9-acre neighbourhood park in Twinbrook, unlit by the City's own answer, and reached on foot because the park has no parking.

The City's table row reads "2 Pickleball Courts (pickleball lines on 1 tennis court; bring your own net)", Lighted "No". That is one tennis court carrying two pickleball games at once, each with a net the players bring. The park's page says the same thing from the tennis end: "two tennis courts (one with pickleball lines)". Two courts is a game rather than a rotation, and with no lights it is a daylight game.

The rest of the park, in the City's description, is a baseball field, a basketball court, a pavilion, a picnic table, a playground, and trails "that wind through a wooded area, linking Gladstone Drive and Baltimore Road". Dogs are welcome on a leash, with waste stations along the trails. The pavilion can be rented, and the City notes that "restrooms are available only with a permit", which means a booking, not a drop-in game.

The parking answer is a stated no, and it is unusual for a parks department to write one: "Calvin Park does not have parking. Access to park amenities is available via pathways connecting to city sidewalks and roads." The City adds that "The park can also be accessed via the bike path along Baltimore Road." So plan to walk or ride in, or park on a street the City does not name. Where the trails come out - Gladstone Drive at one end, Baltimore Road at the other - is the City's own description.

Because the two pickleball courts share one tennis court, a tennis player who arrives first takes both of them. The City says "City recreation programs have priority over the use of the courts, so some may be reserved for class use and closed to the public", and the row's "View Schedule" link has not been read for this page, so which hours are closed for class is not published.

slots.description:
Five pickleball courts painted on three lit tennis courts in a 44.22-acre athletic park and forest preserve, open until 10 p.m. under the lights.

The five is the sum of two lines the City prints in one row of its table: "1 Pickleball Court (pickleball lines on 1 tennis court; use tennis net)" and "4 Pickleball Courts (pickleball lines on 2 tennis courts; bring your own net)", Lighted "Yes". Read literally, that is one tennis court lined for a single pickleball game played over the tennis net, and two more tennis courts lined for two games each with nets the players bring. The park's page describes the same courts as "three lighted tennis courts (complete with pickleball lines - just bring your own net". Because one line says use the tennis net and the other says bring your own, this venue publishes no single net answer.

The park around them is big: 44.22 acres, with three baseball/softball fields, two of them premier fields including Walter Johnson Field with a statue of the pitcher, three lighted basketball courts, a sand volleyball court, batting cages, two pavilions, two playgrounds, grills, drinking fountains and nature trails through the forest to Cabin John Creek.
slots.getting_there:

The US Census address geocoder matched the house number and street as written and answered 20850, and 20850 is the postcode published here, with the disagreement stated rather than resolved. Montgomery County, inside the incorporated place Rockville city.

Parking is stated: "Dogwood Park offers plenty of parking", with "Six accessible parking spaces." in the accessible-features table and the two playgrounds reachable from the parking lots. The City also gives three walk-in routes - "from the south via Grand Oak Way, from the east at the intersection of Cabin John Parkway and West Edmonston Drive, or from the west along New Mark Esplanade". Restrooms are "available only with a permit" for the pavilion.
slots.what_to_expect:
Lit courts and a late finish. The City's rule is dawn to dusk, first-come, first-served, and for lit rows "Lighted courts close at 10 p.m.", so this is one of four Rockville venues where an after-work game is a published possibility rather than a guess. Five courts is enough for a rotation, but only if you brought nets for four of them.

The net arrangement is the thing to understand before you arrive. One tennis court is set up for one pickleball game over the tennis net, which needs nothing from you. The other two tennis courts carry two games each and the City says "bring your own net" for those four. Turn up without a net and you are competing for one court out of five.

As everywhere in Rockville, "City recreation programs have priority over the use of the courts", and the row's schedule link has not been read for this page. These are tennis courts first: a tennis player who arrives first takes a court that would otherwise hold two games. No price, no surface. The lighted basketball courts and premier ballfields share the park, so expect company on an evening.

faqs.a: Five, all on tennis courts, from two lines in the City's row: "1 Pickleball Court (pickleball lines on 1 tennis court; use tennis net)" and "4 Pickleball Courts (pickleball lines on 2 tennis courts; bring your own net)".
Yes. The Lighted column reads Yes, the park page calls them "three lighted tennis courts", and the City says "Lighted courts close at 10 p.m."

faqs.a: For one court, no - it is played over the tennis net. For the other four, yes: "bring your own net". No single net answer is published for the venue.

The City's row reads "4 Pickleball Courts (pickleball lines on 2 tennis courts; bring your own net)", Lighted "No". The park page says "two tennis courts with pickleball lines", and its accessible-features table counts "Two accessible tennis courts."

The City describes the park as "a 30.66-acre park adjoining Thomas Farm Community Center" with a playground, outdoor fitness equipment, a pavilion with tables and grills, paths and trails, a forest preservation area and a multipurpose field, and says it "connects with the 11-mile Millennium Trail allowing quick and easy commuter access". Thomas Farm Community Center itself is one of three centres the City names for "open gym schedules during drop-in hours featuring pickleball", with no court count, so the indoor play next door is named on the city page and not listed.

Dogs are welcome on a leash. The pavilion can be rented, and "restrooms are available only with a permit". The City places the park "on the western side of the Twinbrook neighborhood".

The striped pair exists only in the table, on the one tennis court the park has.

The City describes "a newly constructed rentable pavilion with ADA-accessibility including picnic tables, grills, restrooms and landscaping", a playground installed in 2024, a basketball court, a baseball/softball field and a quarter-mile paved walking path. The park adjoins the Lincoln Park Community Center, one of three centres the City names for drop-in gym pickleball without a court count.

slots.description:
Four dedicated pickleball courts, lit, in a 26.29-acre park at the north end of King Farm, and the venue where the City holds its social play four mornings a week.

The City's row reads "4 Dedicated Pickleball Courts", Lighted "Yes". The park page says "four lighted pickleball courts" and the accessible-features table "Four accessible pickleball courts." - three City statements, one count. With Broome Athletic Park this is one of two Rockville venues where every court was built for pickleball rather than lined onto tennis.

The City's pickleball page adds: "Social play is held at Mattie J.T. Stepanek Park from 10 a.m.-12 p.m. on Mondays, Wednesdays, Fridays, and Sundays", with players rotated "so everyone has a chance to play".

The park opened in 2008 and is named for Mattie J.T. Stepanek, "a poet and peace advocate"; it holds a Peace Garden with a bronze statue of Mattie and his service dog Micah, three outdoor stone chess boards and a labyrinth installed in 2024. Around the courts are three lighted tennis courts, two lighted basketball courts, two premier Bermudagrass fields, a Bankshot court, an outdoor ping pong table, outdoor fitness equipment and a fenced dog park.

The social play sessions are the one busy time the City writes down anywhere in Rockville: 10 a.m. to noon on Mondays, Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays. If you want a game without bringing three friends, those are the mornings to come; if you want the four courts to yourselves, they are the mornings to skip. Beyond that, "City recreation programs have priority over the use of the courts", and the row's "View Schedule" link has not been read for this page.

Three pickleball courts in a 7.4-acre neighbourhood park in Twinbrook, unlit by the City's own answer, and the one row in the City's table that does not say whether its courts are dedicated or lined on tennis.

The row reads "3 Pickleball Courts (bring your own net)", Lighted "No". Every other published row in the table says either "Dedicated" or "pickleball lines on" a tennis court; this one says neither, so the three are counted and left unsplit rather than guessed. The park page lists "pickleball courts (must bring own nets)" among the features and lists no tennis court at all, which is consistent with dedicated courts but is not a statement of it.

The City describes a park that "connects various streets and areas in the Twinbrook Neighborhood", containing the Rockcrest Ballet Center, "a new for 2024 playground", basketball courts, picnic tables, benches and "paved paths connecting Broadwood Avenue to Ardennes Avenue" which "ultimately leads to the Twinbrook Community Center". Three courts is three games at once, and a wait when a fourth group arrives.

What you cannot know from the City's pages is whether you will find pickleball courts or a tennis court with lines on it, because Rockcrest's row is the one that does not say. The absence of a tennis court from the park's feature list points one way, but what publishes is what the operator writes, and the operator has not written it.

"City recreation programs have priority over the use of the courts", and the row's "View Schedule" link has not been read for this page. No price is stated and no surface is named. The courts are outdoor by the heading of the City's table. The playground is new for 2024 in the City's words; the courts carry no date.

The City's row reads "4 Pickleball Courts (pickleball lines on 2 tennis courts; bring your own net)", Lighted "No". Two games per tennis court, nets the players bring, and a stated no on lighting. The park page lists "tennis courts with pickleball lines and a rally wall" among the adjoining grounds, and its accessible-features table counts "Four accessible tennis courts." - four tennis courts on the site, of which the table says two carry pickleball lines. The complex is mostly not about sport. The City lists Glenview Mansion and Cottage, the F. Scott Fitzgerald Theatre, Croydon Creek Nature Center with "120 acres of forest and meadow", formal gardens and a forest preserve, and on the adjoining grounds a playground, picnic areas with tables and grills, artwork and "paved paths with historical signage and information". The courts are one item in a long list, and the page describes the park as "centrally located".

slots.description:
Six pickleball courts - two built for the game and four painted on two lit tennis courts - in a 33.3-acre sports park and forest preserve beside the Rockville Swim and Fitness Center, and the largest set of courts in the city's table.

The City's row prints two lines: "2 Dedicated Pickleball Courts" and "4 Pickleball Courts (pickleball lines on 2 tennis courts; bring your own net)", Lighted "Yes". The park page describes the same six as "two lighted tennis courts with pickleball lines, as well as two dedicated pickleball courts". The Lighted Yes is the row's answer for the venue; the park page attaches the word lighted to the tennis courts and does not repeat it for the dedicated pair, and that is worth knowing before an evening visit.

The City describes a park "next to the Rockville Swim and Fitness Center and Rockville Skate Park" with futsal, soccer and street hockey courts, three lighted basketball courts, three baseball/softball fields, a playground with separate areas for different age groups, picnic tables, paved paths and nature trails. Dogs are welcome on a leash.

Parking is stated: "There are also plenty of parking spaces, so you'll have no trouble finding a spot.", with "Two accessible parking spaces." counted and an accessible path from the parking to the playground. Restrooms are not in the park's feature list, and this page does not add them; the swim centre next door is a separate City facility and was not read for this page.
slots.what_to_expect:
The most courts in Rockville and a late finish. The City's rule is dawn to dusk, first-come, first-served, and for this lit row "Lighted courts close at 10 p.m.", so six courts and an evening window - as much as any published venue in the city offers.

The six split into two kinds. The two dedicated courts are pickleball courts whenever you arrive, and the row says nothing about nets on them. The other four are lines on two tennis courts, "bring your own net", and they become two the moment a tennis game starts. So a group with nets has six courts to aim at; a group without has two.

"City recreation programs have priority over the use of the courts", and the row's "View Schedule" link has not been read for this page. No price is stated and no surface is named. The courts are outdoor by the heading of the City's table. The three lighted basketball courts and three ballfields mean the park will have company on any evening the lights are on.

faqs.a: Six: "2 Dedicated Pickleball Courts" plus "4 Pickleball Courts (pickleball lines on 2 tennis courts; bring your own net)". The park page describes the same six.
